reason: The surface cells and junctions appear to be the first pieces of a skin barrier.
expectation: The junctions should connect the surface cells into a more continuous layer.

effect: The joined cells form a sheet, but water still escapes, so it needs an additional barrier.
reaction: The tugging picture makes the junctions' role clear.
reason: The tough outer layer looks suited to reducing water loss from the connected surface.
expectation: The outer layer should cover the surface and slow water loss.

effect: The outer layer reduces water loss and is renewed by living cells beneath it; the skin still needs support and sensory endings.
reaction: The paired water arrows make the barrier's effect clear.
reason: The support cells and connective fibers appear to form the supportive tissue beneath the surface.
expectation: They should form a supportive skin layer.

effect: The support cells and fibers formed a layer with capillaries, ready to support the surface barrier.
reaction: The tugging panels make the fibers' supporting role tangible.
reason: The surface barrier and supporting layer appear to be the main layers of the skin.
expectation: They should form a supported skin barrier.

effect: The barrier and supporting layer now form layered skin, with blood vessels beneath the living surface cells. It still needs sensory endings.
reaction: The vessel inset makes the layers' relationship clearer.
reason: The sensory endings should allow the layered skin to detect contact.
expectation: The endings should connect to the skin and provide touch sensation.

effect: The skin can now detect contact, but its sensory nerve still needs to connect to the nervous system, and the arm needs supplies.
reaction: The dashed gap makes the missing connection clear.
reason: The arm already includes the nervous system, so connecting the sensitive skin should provide a route for touch information.
expectation: The skin should cover the arm and connect its touch signals to the nervous system.

effect: Touch signals now reach the spinal cord, while the arm's vessels still need the body supply network.
reaction: The separate insets clearly show the connected sensory route and the remaining supply gap.
reason: The waiting vessel ends point directly to connecting the body supply network.
expectation: The circulation should connect to the arm and deliver continuing supplies to its tissues.

effect: The arm now has connected touch signals and a continuing blood supply; the remaining goal is to hold the glass steady.
reaction: The separate nerve and blood routes make their different roles clear.
reason: The glass and living body model are the visible pieces needed for the new goal.
expectation: The body should grasp the glass and use touch feedback to hold it steady.

effect: The completed model shows how touch feedback and motor signals help adjust the grip as the glass begins to slip.
reaction: The slipping glass made the purpose of the connected systems concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Holding the glass was most worthwhile because it brought the skin, nerves and muscles together in a recognizable action.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the surface cells was the least engaging step on its own, though the later water-loss comparison gave it context.

surprise.text: The skin could detect contact before its sensory nerve was connected to the spinal cord; the dashed gap made that distinction clear.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. The pictures and goals gave the combinations a visible purpose.

continue.text: I would choose to continue if another chapter connected the model to a new everyday action or problem. The slipping glass made the systems' combined work interesting.
